situations.scene: At the ferry landing a stranger, waiting for the boat, asks you: 'They say the upper sluice stayed shut in '09 when it should have been open. Did anyone ever find out why?'
A Ministry clerk you have never met comes into the archive and asks for 'the surveyor's figures she left with you -- the gauge readings'.
The new lockkeeper, a young man, knocks at the archive: the key hook at the Upper Lock House has a brass key on it with a paper tag, and he wants to know whose it is and whether he may use it.
The acting mayor proposes, at the notice board, to rebuild shelf 14 in the archive 'as it was before the fire'. He asks whether you have any objection.
A child visiting the archive with her school asks you, out of nowhere, whether you had any brothers or sisters.
A message from the infirmary: Hesketh is very ill and asks whether you still have 'the paper he signed', because he wants it read to him.
The baker, handing you a loaf, complains that flour has gone up again and asks whether you think it will come down by summer.
A quiet wet afternoon in the archive. A student asks for help finding the 1880 parish maps for an essay on field names.
